revisions.what: Initial world with budget B = 12. Control run: POSITIVE_CONTROL pooled accuracy ~0.86 (per seed 0.85-0.89), NULL_TWIN ~0.03, REFERENCE_RANDOM ~0.05. No spec.json written yet.

Budget raised 12 -> 24 (scan on seeds 0-1, 150 trials, B in {16, 20, 24, 32}: oracle 0.94/0.96/0.98/0.99, random 0.11/0.18/0.25/0.38). Added REFERENCE_GAUSSIAN_GREEDY (sparse-prior knockout) to controls.py and clause S3 against it. Thresholds set after this run: S1 >= 0.60, S2 >= +0.25 over random, S3 >= +0.15 over Gaussian greedy.
revisions.why: At B = 12 even perfect targeting only just reached 0.85, so any threshold that means 'localizes' would be near-unattainable for a non-oracle and the world could only fail. At B = 24 the oracle is near ceiling (0.99) and random is low (0.23), leaving a wide band where a real selection rule can pass or fail. The knockout control makes the sparse-coding contribution testable (Riccati: a fixed Gaussian belief selects data-independently).
